The detector identifies all three CIVO-positive runs (TPR = 3/3). Detection timing depends on collapse dynamics. For gradual-onset collapse (008d seed 0), the detector fires at 45K, one checkpoint (10K steps) before evaluation crosses the 50% catastrophic threshold, providing an actionable intervention window. For late-onset collapse (seed 3), detection occurs 55K steps before any evaluation decline begins, because the value-evaluation ratio already exhibits the characteristic acceleration pattern during an early transient phase. For sudden-onset collapse (010b), where evaluation drops 80% in a single checkpoint interval, no metric-based detector can provide advance warning; the detector fires reactively at the next checkpoint (65K), confirming the event within one monitoring cycle.

The single false positive (009c) is instructive: this run uses no trained duration embedding yet exhibits late-stage value divergence coupled with evaluation decline (359 to 148 over 30K steps), a genuine pathology unrelated to CIVO. The detector correctly flags the value-performance dissociation pattern; the attribution to CIVO specifically requires additional context (whether temporal conditioning is active). Two observations support framing this as a useful alert rather than a pure false alarm. First, the run is genuinely degrading. Second, the 60K step gap between positive-case triggers (45-65K) and the false positive trigger (105K) is itself diagnostic: CIVO accelerates value divergence, producing earlier detection.

Three constraints bound the current detector's applicability. First, the acceleration condition assumes monotonically increasing overestimation during CIVO onset. In runs where value excess oscillates before stabilizing (as observed in the self-correcting trajectory of 009b), the detector may fire late or not at all. The 009b run reached NVE $\geq$ 1.5$\times$ transiently but then self-corrected without collapse; the detector's silence here is appropriate (no collapse to predict), yet a modified variant that oscillates longer before collapsing could evade detection until the acceleration condition is finally met.

Second, the detector identifies a *pattern* (rising value-evaluation ratio with declining performance) rather than a *mechanism*. Run 009c demonstrates that non-CIVO pathologies can produce the same signature. The detector is best understood as a "value health monitor" whose alerts warrant investigation, not as a definitive CIVO diagnosis. Disambiguating CIVO from other value pathologies requires checking whether temporal conditioning is active, a trivial additional filter in practice but one that the core algorithm does not enforce.

Third, our validation set comprises eight runs across two environments (Walker Walk, HalfCheetah) with one architecture (DreamerV3/RSSM). While the detection logic is environment-agnostic (it operates on normalized ratios), the threshold values ($\tau_\text{mag} = 0.49$, $\tau_\text{vel} = 0.1$) were calibrated on this experimental suite. 1	# Section 5.3: Online CIVO Detection
2	
3	## Motivation
4	
5	The Normalized Value Excess (NVE) metric introduced in Section 4 quantifies CIVO severity by comparing the value-to-evaluation ratio against a reference baseline that does not employ temporal abstraction. This comparison is informative for post-hoc diagnosis but unusable during deployment: no practitioner has access to a converged baseline run while training a new agent. A metric that requires a completed control experiment to interpret cannot serve as an early warning. We therefore ask whether the *dynamics* of value overestimation, rather than its absolute magnitude relative to an external reference, contain sufficient signal to detect CIVO onset in real time. The answer, as we show below, is affirmative. By tracking the trajectory of the value-to-evaluation ratio across checkpoints, a lightweight rule-based detector can flag dangerous overestimation 15K to 60K steps before performance collapse, using only quantities available within a single run.
6	
7	## Detection Algorithm
8	
9	The detector monitors a scalar signal $r_t = \bar{V}_t / \bar{E}_t$, the ratio of mean predicted value to mean episodic evaluation at checkpoint $t$.
